page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-6 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g4 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture with 6 dedicated vCPUs and 22.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.67 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes a fractional GPU allocation consisting of one-eighth of an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture family, providing 12 GB of dedicated VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The primary tradeoff of this instance is its fractional GPU allocation, which provides access to modern Ada Lovelace architecture features at a lower entry point than a full dedicated GPU, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not saturate a full physical card.

The g4-standard-6 is designed for workloads such as light 3D rendering, remote workstation hosting, video transcoding, and low-intensity machine learning inference. Its balanced ratio of 6 dedicated vCPUs to 22.0 GB of RAM, combined with the fractional RTX Pro 6000 GPU, supports entry-level graphics tasks and CUDA-accelerated applications without the overhead of a full GPU.
